question:
(a) Explain the effect of forward bias and reverse bias on a $p\text{-}n$ junction.
(b) Hence justify why a semiconductor diode conducts easily in forward bias but offers high resistance in reverse bias.

options.A:
(a) In forward bias p-side is connected to negative and n-side to positive, increasing barrier and depletion width; reverse bias does the opposite.
(b) The diode conducts easily in reverse bias due to large majority-carrier current.
options.B:
(a) Both forward and reverse bias reduce the barrier and depletion width.
(b) Hence a diode offers equal resistance in both directions.
options.C:
(a) In forward bias p-side is connected to positive and n-side to negative, reducing barrier potential and narrowing the depletion layer. In reverse bias the connections are reversed, increasing the barrier and widening the layer.
(b) Hence majority carriers cross easily in forward bias and a large current flows, whereas in reverse bias majority carriers are blocked and only a tiny minority-carrier current flows; the diode has low forward and high reverse resistance.
options.D:
(a) Forward bias has no effect on carrier movement, while reverse bias removes all ions.
(b) A diode conducts due to gravity in forward bias.
